exposure: publicly reporting a statewide fetal growth restriction (FGR) performance indicator
outcome: rate of detection for severe cases of small for gestational age (SGA)
admissions to neonatal intensive care unit (NICU)
cohort: The study included 1,231,415 singleton births at >=32 weeks of gestation in Victoria, Australia, from 2000 to 2017.
finding: Publicly reporting an FGR performance indicator was associated with improved detection of severe SGA and a decrease in the stillbirth rate, but also an increase in iatrogenic birth for babies with normal growth.
mod_finding: The public reporting was associated with an increase in iatrogenic birth (likely leading to changes in mode of delivery) for babies with normal growth.
